title: Wiring of premises
summary: The SA wiring code for low-voltage installations. It covers cable sizing, earthing, protection and the certificate of compliance.
tip: Every PV and battery install we do needs a certificate of compliance against this before handover.

title: Small-scale embedded generation
summary: Extra low-voltage wiring rules for a small generator, including PV, connected to a normal premises supply.
tip: A rooftop PV or hybrid inverter is signed off under this together with SANS 10142-1, not as a separate habit.

title: Medium-voltage installations
summary: The wiring code for medium-voltage premises installations, separate from the low-voltage code.
tip: A site with a medium-voltage intake or transformer is not covered by the low-voltage rules we use on a normal PV board.

title: Utility interface
summary: The utility interface rules for connecting a small embedded generator, including a PV or battery inverter, to the grid.
tip: We do not commission a grid-tied inverter until the utility has accepted the connection against this interface.

title: Simplified LV connection
summary: A simpler set of utility connection checks for small generators connected on the low-voltage network.
tip: Before we order the inverter, we confirm with the municipality or Eskom whether this site uses the simplified path or the full interface.

title: Quality of supply
summary: The NRS series that defines the quality of the power the utility supplies, including voltage level, dips and interruptions.
tip: When a site reports dips or flicker, we describe them in these terms to the utility, and we do not set our own limits.

title: PV documentation and tests
summary: The inspection, commissioning tests and documentation required for a grid-connected PV system.
tip: We complete the test sheets and the system record on site, and we hand them over with the job.

title: PV array design
summary: Design requirements for the PV array, including strings, array cable, protection and earthing of the array.
tip: We fix the string layout and the array cable before the modules go down, so we are not reworking a finished roof.

title: PV module qualification
summary: Design qualification and type-approval tests for terrestrial PV modules.
tip: We ask for this qualification on the module datasheet before we buy modules for a roof.

title: PV module safety
summary: Safety qualification for PV modules, covering how they are built and the safety tests they must pass.
tip: Design qualification and safety qualification are separate. We want both before we place a module order.

title: PV in the LV installation
summary: Low-voltage installation requirements for a solar PV power supply in a building.
tip: The PV supply has to meet these installation rules as well as the rest of the building wiring.

title: Protection against shock
summary: The basic low-voltage rules for protection against electric shock.
tip: Earthing, automatic disconnection and barriers on our boards and battery cabinets follow this.

title: PV converter safety
summary: Safety requirements for power converters used in PV systems, including inverters.
tip: We do not install a PV inverter that has no credible safety listing to this standard.

title: Anti-islanding test method
summary: The test procedure that checks a grid-connected PV inverter stops supplying a grid that has been disconnected.
tip: We leave anti-islanding enabled, and we confirm the inverter stops when the grid side is opened.

title: Industrial lithium safety
summary: Safety requirements for lithium cells and batteries used in industrial applications, including stationary storage.
tip: On a battery datasheet we look for this safety standard, not only a product brochure.

title: Battery installation safety
summary: Safety requirements for installing secondary batteries, including layout, ventilation and protection.
tip: Ventilation, access and isolation of the battery room or cabinet are part of the install, not a later snag.

title: Electrical energy storage
summary: The IEC series for electrical energy storage systems, from planning through to the system itself.
tip: When a client asks for a battery, we treat it as a storage system under this series, not as a loose pack of cells.

title: Energy storage systems
summary: A US safety listing for energy storage systems and equipment. It is a reference, not a South African law.
tip: If a cabinet claims a UL listing, we check that the listing covers the whole system and not only a cell inside it.

title: Thermal runaway fire test
summary: A test method for how a fire spreads through a battery energy storage system. The report is evidence, not a claim that a fire cannot start.
tip: When battery spacing or the room layout is being decided, we ask for this test report instead of guessing a clearance.

title: Stationary storage installs
summary: A US installation standard for stationary energy storage systems. We use it as a reference unless the specification calls it up.
tip: It is a checklist for where the battery sits and how it can be reached in a fire. It does not replace SANS 10142-1.

title: DER interconnection
summary: IEEE rules for connecting distributed energy resources to the power system. Our utilities use NRS, not this, as the local requirement.
tip: Inverter menus often use IEEE names. The settings we leave on site still have to match NRS 097 and the local utility.

title: UPS systems
summary: The series for uninterruptible power systems, covering safety and how performance is specified.
tip: A battery inverter that can run a load off-grid is not automatically a UPS. We check what the client actually specified.

title: Generating sets
summary: The ISO series for engine-driven AC generating sets, covering ratings and performance.
tip: We read the genset rating and duty on the nameplate before we use it in the changeover or the PLC scheme.

title: Rotating machines
summary: The IEC series for rotating electrical machines, covering motors and generators and their ratings.
tip: When we start, protect or monitor a motor or generator, we take the rating and the duty from the machine data, not from a guess.

title: LV switchgear
summary: Low-voltage switchgear and controlgear, including circuit-breakers, contactors and disconnectors.
tip: We use a device only for the current, voltage and duty on its label, and we do not use an AC device on a DC string.

title: LV assemblies
summary: Requirements for low-voltage switchgear assemblies, meaning the built panel, not only the parts inside it.
tip: A board we design and populate is an assembly. Listed components do not by themselves make the finished board compliant.

title: IP ratings
summary: The IP code for how well an enclosure keeps out solid objects and water. The two digits mean different things.
tip: An outdoor inverter or a roof box needs the IP rating the site requires. We read both digits on the label.

title: Surge protective devices
summary: Requirements for low-voltage surge protective devices, including selection and application.
tip: We fit surge protection on the PV DC side and the AC side, and we bond it as this series requires.

title: Lightning protection
summary: The SA standard for protection of structures, and the electrical services on them, against lightning.
tip: A roof with modules, frames and DC cable needs a lightning protection design. The array frame is not that design by itself.

title: Hazardous areas
summary: Requirements for equipment and wiring in explosive atmospheres.
tip: If a battery room, fuel store or genset area is a hazardous zone, we do not put ordinary electrical gear in that zone.

title: Electromagnetic compatibility
summary: The EMC series. It sets how much a product may emit and how much interference it must withstand.
tip: When a PLC resets next to a drive or an inverter, we check cable route, screen and earth before we change the program.

title: Power electronic converters
summary: Safety requirements for power electronic converter systems, wider than PV inverters alone.
tip: Storage converters and drives fall here too. We ask which safety standard the box was built to.

title: Utility automation comms
summary: Communication networks and data models for substation and utility automation.
tip: If a protection relay or grid meter uses IEC 61850, we get its point list. A Modbus map does not describe it.

title: Telecontrol over TCP
summary: A utility telecontrol protocol that carries remote-control messages over a standard TCP/IP network.
tip: We do not offer the municipality this link unless we have the protocol stack and an agreed point list.

title: PLC general information
summary: The overview of programmable controllers and of the IEC 61131 family of standards.
tip: It states what the PLC standards cover. The language we write and the hardware tests are in the later parts.

title: PLC equipment requirements
summary: Equipment requirements and tests for the PLC hardware itself.
tip: We check the temperature and supply rating of a PLC or remote I/O before we put it in a hot outdoor panel.

title: PLC programming languages
summary: The standard PLC programming languages, including the structured text used in PC Worx and PLCnext.
tip: We write structured text the next person can follow, with signal names that say what they are.

title: Control system security
summary: Security requirements for industrial automation and control systems, including network zones and who may connect.
tip: We change default passwords, we do not leave remote access open, and we do not put the PLC on the site guest network.

title: RS-485 electrical layer
summary: The electrical specification for a balanced multipoint serial link. Modbus RTU usually runs on it.
tip: We wire it as one daisy chain, we terminate the two ends, and we connect the cable shield to earth at one point only.

title: Modbus application protocol
summary: The application protocol for reading and writing coils and registers, over a serial link or over TCP.
tip: The protocol defines the frame. We take the register map, including any scaling, from that device's manual.

title: Energy efficiency in buildings
summary: Energy-efficiency requirements for buildings in South Africa.
tip: A PV or storage job can be asked to support a building energy target. We check whether the architect already has one.

title: Building energy usage
summary: The National Building Regulations part that sets energy-usage requirements for buildings.
tip: Hot water, lighting and the building envelope sit in this document. Our plant does not replace those requirements.

title: Safe work and the CoC
summary: The occupational health and safety law. Its electrical installation regulations require a certificate of compliance for the wiring.
tip: We lock out and prove the circuit is dead, and we do not sign a certificate for work we did not inspect.

title: Regulator registration
summary: The National Energy Regulator of South Africa. Some generation needs a licence or a registration before it may operate.
tip: We ask which NERSA approval this plant and this utility need before we run the system in parallel with the grid.

title: Modbus word and byte order
summary: A 32-bit value can be split across two Modbus registers, and devices do not all place the high word in the same register.
tip: We check one known value, such as a serial number or a voltage we can measure, before we trust the register map.

title: Scaling a register
summary: A Modbus register is often a raw integer. The device manual states the scale that turns it into engineering units.
tip: We apply that scale in one place in the structured text, then we check the result with a meter.

title: Cold-morning string voltage
summary: A PV module's open-circuit voltage is higher when the cells are cold than the value given for standard test conditions.
tip: We size each string so that cold open-circuit voltage stays within the inverter's maximum DC voltage.

title: Anti-islanding
summary: If the grid supply is lost, the inverter must stop exporting so the disconnected line is not kept live.
tip: We prove the inverter stops when we open the grid-side breaker. A setting on the screen is not that test.

title: SOC and SOH
summary: State of charge is how full the battery is now. State of health is how much of its original capacity remains.
tip: We do not tell the client the battery is healthy because the state of charge reads full.

title: C-rate
summary: C-rate is the charge or discharge current compared with the battery's capacity. A higher rate is more current for the same pack.
tip: We stay inside the charge and discharge rates the manufacturer publishes for that battery.

title: Peak shaving
summary: The battery supplies the site during peaks so the power drawn from the grid does not set a new maximum demand.
tip: We agree the demand ceiling with the client, and the PLC alarms before the site reaches it.

title: Time-of-use arbitrage
summary: The battery is charged when the energy tariff is low and discharged when the tariff is high.
tip: We put the tariff seasons and time bands in the PLC where they can be read, and we check them against the current municipal tariff.
